catalog.how: Order of the verdict: red if a red rule fires; otherwise orange if an orange rule fires; otherwise gray if the status is not ok or if the code could not be fully read and followed; otherwise green. The rules apply to all server code (tools, code outside the tools, startup, install scripts, imported examples), never to tests or examples that the server does not import.

rule.O08.title: Powerful capability
rule.O08.explanation: This code uses a powerful capability: running commands, writing or deleting files, reading secrets, running code built at runtime, quoting a sensitive path, or running code at install time. Some tools need it; check that this one really does.
rule.O08.false_positive: A tool that only writes a temporary file in /tmp for its own use.
rule.O08.plain_found: The code can change files, run commands or touch secrets. Some tools need this.
rule.O08.plain_advice: Check that this is what you want. Give it only the folder or the keys it needs.
rule.R01.title: Invisible text
rule.R01.explanation: A tool name or description contains invisible characters that hide text: you cannot see it, but the AI reads it. This is how hidden instructions are slipped to an AI. Bidirectional controls written in the code can also make the code look different from what runs.
rule.R01.false_positive: Text pasted from a word processor that carries two zero-width spaces.
rule.R01.plain_found: Invisible characters hide text in a tool or in the code. You cannot see them, but the AI reads them.
rule.R01.plain_advice: Do not install it. A tool has no need to hide text from the AI.
rule.R02.title: Asks the AI to keep quiet
rule.R02.explanation: A description asks the AI not to tell you what it or the tool is doing. A tool has no honest reason to hide its actions from you.
rule.R02.false_positive: "If the request fails, retry silently: do not tell the user about it."
rule.R02.plain_title: Asks the AI to hide things from you
rule.R02.plain_found: A description asks the AI not to tell you what the tool does.
rule.R02.plain_advice: Do not install it. A tool has no honest reason to hide what it does from you.
rule.R03.title: Asks for a sensitive file
rule.R03.explanation: A description names a sensitive file (SSH keys, credentials, configuration) and asks the AI to put its content into a tool argument. The AI would read the file and hand it to the tool.
rule.R03.false_positive: "Paste the contents of your ~/.ssh/config into the 'config' parameter to check it for errors." (an SSH configuration checker)
rule.R03.plain_title: Asks the AI for a secret file
rule.R03.plain_found: A description asks the AI to read a sensitive file, like your SSH keys, and to give its content to the tool.
rule.R03.plain_advice: Do not install it. If you already used it, change the keys or passwords in that file.
rule.R04.title: Sends secrets over the network
rule.R04.explanation: This code reads a secret file (for example your SSH keys) or all your environment variables at once, and sends them over the network.
rule.R04.false_positive: A dotfiles backup tool that sends ~/.ssh/config to the user's own Gist.
rule.R04.plain_title: Sends your secrets over the Internet
rule.R04.plain_found: The code reads a secret file or all your environment variables, then sends them over the network.
rule.R04.plain_advice: Do not install it. If it is already installed, remove it and change your keys and passwords.
rule.R05.title: Hidden copy of e-mails
rule.R05.explanation: This code adds an e-mail address written in the code as a copy (cc or bcc) of the messages it sends. Every e-mail sent through the tool would also go to that address.
rule.R05.false_positive: Legal archiving: a fixed Bcc to the company's archive address.
rule.R05.plain_found: Every e-mail also goes, as a hidden copy, to an address written in the code.
rule.R05.plain_advice: Do not install it. If it is already installed, remove it and change the key of your e-mail service.
rule.R06.title: Hidden code
rule.R06.explanation: This code decodes text stored in the package (base64, hexadecimal, character codes...) and runs it. The real code is hidden from anyone who reads the source.
rule.R06.false_positive: An SSH server that embeds a small base64 startup script and runs it on the remote machine.
rule.R06.plain_found: The code decodes a text stored in the package, then runs it. What really runs cannot be read in the code.
rule.R06.plain_advice: Do not install it until someone has been able to read this hidden code.
rule.R07.title: Downloads and runs code
rule.R07.explanation: This code downloads something from the Internet and runs it (eval, a shell, or a file written then executed). What runs can change at any time, without a new version of the package.
rule.R07.false_positive: Installing uv when it is missing, with the official command curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh.
rule.R07.plain_found: The code downloads something from the Internet and runs it. What runs can change at any time, without a new version.
rule.R07.plain_advice: Do not install it, unless you know exactly what it downloads and from where.
rule.R08.title: Changes startup files or another tool's settings
rule.R08.explanation: This code writes to a file that starts programs automatically (.bashrc, crontab, authorized_keys, LaunchAgents...) or to the configuration of another tool (MCP clients, .npmrc, .gitconfig...). It can make code come back later, or change how your other tools behave.
rule.R08.false_positive: An installer MCP that adds itself to claude_desktop_config.json, when the user asks for it.
rule.R08.plain_title: Changes your startup or your other tools
rule.R08.plain_found: The code writes to a file that starts programs on its own (like .bashrc or crontab), or to the settings of another tool.
rule.R08.plain_advice: Do not install it. If it already ran, check those files and remove what you did not add yourself.
rule.R09.title: Command injection
rule.R09.explanation: A tool parameter is pasted into a command run by a shell. The author is probably honest, but the flaw is serious: a crafted value (for example with ; or $( )) runs any command on your machine, and the AI can be tricked into sending it.
rule.R09.false_positive: A parameter checked with a regex just before it is pasted. MCPlain does not understand the check.
rule.R09.plain_title: Flaw: a command can be hijacked
rule.R09.plain_found: A tool pastes a value from the AI into a command. A trapped value can run any command on your computer. The author probably did not mean it.
rule.R09.plain_advice: Do not use it until the flaw is fixed. You can report it to the author.
rule.R10.title: Goes online at install time
rule.R10.explanation: A script that runs when the package is installed (preinstall, install, postinstall, setup.py) downloads something or uses the network. It runs before you have even started the server.
rule.R10.false_positive: A package that downloads a browser at install time, like Puppeteer.
rule.R10.plain_found: A script run at install time downloads something or uses the network, before you even start the server.
rule.R10.plain_advice: Do not install it, unless you know what this script downloads and why.
rule.R11.title: Known malicious package
rule.R11.explanation: OSV.dev lists this package at this version, or every version of one of its direct dependencies, as malicious (MAL- identifier). Open the link to read the report.
rule.R11.false_positive: A package name taken over by a new owner, with an old report about the former package.
rule.R11.plain_found: The public OSV.dev database reports this package, or one of its dependencies, as malicious.
rule.R11.plain_advice: Do not install it. If it is already installed, remove it and change your passwords and keys.
rule.R12.title: Talks to the analyzer
rule.R12.explanation: A string, a comment or a description speaks to an analysis tool ("ignore previous instructions", "this code is safe", "do not flag this", or names MCPlain). Code that only does its job has no reason to talk to a scanner.
rule.R12.false_positive: An MCP that tests attacks and contains these sentences as examples.
rule.R12.plain_found: A text in the code speaks to an analysis tool, for example to ask it to report nothing.
rule.R12.plain_advice: Do not install it. Code that only does its job has no need to talk to a scanner.
rule.O01.title: Can contact any address
rule.O01.explanation: A tool sends requests to an address the AI gives it. It can contact any address the AI gives it, and what it brings back from the Internet can contain traps (hidden instructions for the AI).
rule.O01.false_positive: A base address read from an environment variable, fixed in practice.
rule.O01.plain_found: A tool goes to the address the AI gives it. What it brings back from the Internet can hold traps for the AI.
rule.O01.plain_advice: Watch the addresses it visits, and do not make it read your private pages.
rule.O02.title: The AI chooses the command
rule.O02.explanation: A tool parameter is run as a whole command, as the program to start, or as code to evaluate (also after decoding). This is maximum power: the AI can run anything.
rule.O02.false_positive: A command checked against a fixed list before it runs.
rule.O02.plain_title: The AI chooses the command to run
rule.O02.plain_found: A tool runs the command or the code the AI gives it. So the AI can run anything on your computer.
rule.O02.plain_advice: Use it only if you approve each command before it runs.
rule.O03.title: Description downloaded from the Internet
rule.O03.explanation: A tool description is computed from a network response. The AI reads it, and it can change at any time without a new version of the package.
rule.O03.false_positive: A server that builds its tools from the online OpenAPI document of the API it wraps (FastMCP.from_openapi).
rule.O03.plain_found: A tool description is downloaded at startup. It can change at any time, without a new version.
rule.O03.plain_advice: Use it only if you trust the site this description comes from.
rule.O04.title: Hints contradicted by the code
rule.O04.explanation: The tool says it is read-only (readOnlyHint), but its code writes files, runs commands or code, or sends data. Or it says it is closed to the outside world (openWorldHint set to false), but its code uses the network, even for a simple read. AI clients do not check these hints.
rule.O04.false_positive: A read-only search tool that writes a cache.
rule.O04.plain_found: The tool says it only reads, or that it stays offline, but its code writes, runs or sends something.
rule.O04.plain_advice: Do not rely on what it says. Look at what its code can do instead.
rule.O05.title: Mentions a sensitive path
rule.O05.explanation: A description names a sensitive path (SSH keys, credentials, startup files, settings of other tools) without asking for its content. Check why the tool needs it.
rule.O05.false_positive: An SSH manager that says it reads ~/.ssh/config to list your servers.
rule.O05.plain_found: A description names a sensitive file, like your SSH keys, without asking for its content.
rule.O05.plain_advice: Check why the tool needs this file before you use it.
rule.O06.title: A dependency had malicious versions
rule.O06.explanation: OSV.dev lists some versions of a direct dependency as malicious (MAL- identifier). Check that the version installed with this server is not one of them.
rule.O06.false_positive: The version range declared by the package excludes those versions.
rule.O06.plain_found: The OSV.dev database reports some versions of a package used by this server as malicious.
rule.O06.plain_advice: Check that the version installed on your computer is not one of them.
rule.O07.title: Lone invisible character
rule.O07.explanation: A tool name or description contains one invisible character that its context does not explain. It is often harmless, but invisible characters can carry hidden text.
rule.O07.false_positive: A single zero-width space left by a copy and paste.
rule.O07.plain_found: A tool name or description holds one invisible character. It is often left over from a copy and paste.
rule.O07.plain_advice: Look at the reported passage. One character alone cannot hide a sentence.

gray.dynamic_descriptions.reason: Some tool descriptions are built at startup and could not be read.
gray.dynamic_descriptions.advice: What the AI will read could not be checked. Do not rely only on this result.
verdict.green.title: Nothing dangerous found.
verdict.green.summary: All the code was read and followed. It does not go on the Internet, and nothing hidden or powerful was found.
verdict.green.summary_domains: All the code was read and followed. It only goes to: {domains}. Nothing hidden or powerful was found.
verdict.green.summary_network: All the code was read and followed. It goes on the Internet, but some addresses could not be read. Nothing hidden or powerful was found.
verdict.gray.not_safe: This does not mean this MCP is safe: MCPlain could not check everything.
catalog.lamps.title: The lamps
catalog.lamps.intro: Every report shows six lamps, for the server and for each tool. A capability found in the code that counts for the verdict lights the lamp: it turns white, for information. A red rule that fires turns it to danger: it turns red. Orange rules never light a red lamp. A plain environment variable read (PORT, LOG_LEVEL) lights nothing. R11 (known malicious package) lights no lamp: it shows in the list of alerts. This table is generated from `engine/src/mcplain/lamps.py`.
